image.name: Caturus
image.subsector: Integrated natural gas and LNG platform
image.description: Caturus is an integrated U.S. natural-gas and LNG platform whose legal parent is Caturus Holdco, LLC, renamed from SoTex HoldCo in August 2025. The platform combines Caturus Energy's Texas upstream production with the controlled 9.5 mtpa Commonwealth LNG export project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. After the May 14, 2026 CPP Investments closing, regulatory filings support a direct governance cap table of 52.6% Kimmeridge-managed interests, 24.1% Mubadala, 22.8% CPP Investments and 0.5% Caturus management. CPP also has a disclosed economic look-through through Kimmeridge-managed funds, but that indirect interest carries no additional governance and public CPP percentages use a different aggregation basis; the 22.8% direct interest is therefore used for the ownership row. Kimmeridge's exact fund allocation and CPP's primary-versus-secondary mix are not publicly disclosed. Caturus reported more than 1 Bcfe per day of net production across approximately 280,000 net acres after the Galvan Ranch acquisition, while Commonwealth LNG reached FID and closed project financing in May 2026. Caturus Energy and Commonwealth LNG are subordinate operating subsidiaries/projects, not separate manager-level PortCos, and project financiers are not parent owners. No later platform sale, owner exit, cancellation or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Pacifico Sur
aliases: Concesionaria Autopista Guadalajara Tepic, S.A. de C.V.
image.description: Pacifico Sur is the operating toll-road concession held through Concesionaria Autopista Guadalajara Tepic, S.A. de C.V. (CAGT). Its 309.6-kilometer network in Jalisco and Nayarit includes the Guadalajara–Tepic toll road, the South Guadalajara Bypass and the Tepic Bypass, serving freight, tourism and other toll-paying road users under a long-duration user-pay concession. A definitive agreement was announced on October 2, 2018 and the direct purchase of 49% of CAGT closed on May 15, 2019, leaving IDEAL with 51%, CPP Investments with 29% and Ontario Teachers' with 20%. A 2020 modification extended the concession to 60 years from November 30, 2011, implying expiry in November 2071. Pacifico Sur remains a separate direct PortCo from IDEAL Group and Autopista Arco Norte, and no later direct-stake sale, concession transfer or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: CARMA Corp.
image.description: CARMA Corp. provides utility submetering, billing, collections, consumption reporting and on-site technical services for multi-residential, commercial and institutional properties. The company traces its predecessor operations to 1977 and was formed as CARMA Corp. through the August 2019 amalgamation of Carma Industries Inc. and Carma Billing Services Inc. CVC DIF agreed to acquire CARMA from TerraNova through DIF Infrastructure VIII on September 15, 2025, and industry-association reporting confirms the sale closed in December 2025. The disclosed acquisition vehicle is DIF Infra 8 Canada Holdco 2 Ltd.; the exact closing day, acquired stake and any management or family rollover are not publicly disclosed. CARMA operated more than 135,000 units across more than 1,000 buildings at signing and was reported to have approximately 350,000 meters installed across North America by June 2026. Spectrum, Priority Submetering, Undercurrent and Greensource remain operating businesses beneath CARMA rather than separate manager-level PortCos. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: ENFRA
image.subsector: Energy solutions and building infrastructure services
image.description: ENFRA, LLC designs, builds, finances and operates energy, engineering and building-infrastructure solutions for healthcare, higher-education, government, commercial and industrial customers. The company provides engineering, construction, commissioning, maintenance, asset management, optimization, resilience and energy-as-a-service solutions. ENFRA is the same continuing legal entity formerly named Bernhard, LLC; the legal name changed effective May 1, 2025 without changing the entity, EIN, ownership, legal structure or contracts. DIF Infrastructure VI agreed to acquire Bernhard in October 2021 and the sale closed on December 2, 2021. ENFRA continues to identify CVC DIF as its majority owner; the exact fund stake, management rollover percentage and acquisition SPV are not publicly disclosed. The company traces its predecessor heritage to 1919, is headquartered in Metairie, Louisiana and reports operations across 18 states. Subsidiaries, tuck-ins and customer energy-as-a-service projects remain beneath ENFRA unless separate manager ownership is proven. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: JW Water Holdings, LLC
image.description: JW Water Holdings, LLC is a regulated water and wastewater utility platform serving more than 50,000 customers in Arizona. CVC DIF completed the acquisition of JW Water's ten-utility platform and eight Robson utilities through DIF Infrastructure VII in November 2024. Pima became a wholly owned JW Water subsidiary on November 20, 2024, and current company and Arizona Corporation Commission materials show the acquired utilities operating beneath the integrated JW Water platform. Public sources do not disclose CVC DIF's exact ownership percentage or a separate acquisition SPV. Later Pima and other utility consolidations are internal legal and regulatory reorganizations, not manager-level ownership transfers. No later sale, sponsor exit or signed pending manager-level transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: ValorC3 Data Centers
image.subsector: Colocation, cloud and regional data centers
image.description: ValorC3 Data Centers is the operating name of Tonaquint Data Centers, LLC, a regional U.S. data-center platform providing colocation, private cloud, connectivity, disaster recovery, backup and build-to-suit capacity. The platform serves enterprise, channel and hyperscale customers from St. George, Utah, Boise, Idaho and Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. CVC DIF acquired a majority interest through DIF CIF III in December 2022; management retained a minority interest, while exact percentages and the legal closing day were not publicly disclosed. Tonaquint acquired EdgeX in November 2023 and began operating as ValorC3 on January 20, 2025 without creating a new company. Current materials report 19 MW of operating capacity plus a 10 MW Boise facility under development and a second 10 MW facility planned. A 2026 company financing announcement still identified CVC DIF as sponsor, and no later sale, transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Beanfield Metroconnect
image.subsector: Metro fiber broadband and enterprise connectivity
image.description: Beanfield Metroconnect, legally Beanfield Technologies Inc., builds, owns and operates metropolitan fibre networks and provides residential broadband, business connectivity, private networks, cloud connectivity and colocation services in Canada. The platform serves residential and multi-dwelling-unit customers, enterprises, carriers and data centres across Toronto, Montreal, Ottawa and Vancouver, with additional points of presence in Calgary, New York and Seattle. Public transaction materials reported approximately 4,000 kilometres of fibre connecting roughly 4,000 commercial buildings and more than 170,000 residential units in 2023; current scale was not publicly disclosed. Digital Colony Partners acquired Beanfield in November 2019. OMERS Infrastructure completed a minority investment on September 15, 2023, after which DigitalBridge remained the majority owner. OpenFace was integrated into Beanfield, and Beanfield acquired Aptum's metro-network assets rather than Aptum itself. Current DigitalBridge and OMERS materials continue to list Beanfield, and no Beanfield-specific sale, ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Invenergy AMPCI Thermal Power
image.description: Invenergy AMPCI Thermal Power LLC is a 50/50 joint venture that owns a portfolio of dispatchable power-generation assets across the United States and Canada. InfraBridge holds one half through the legacy AMP Capital Global Infrastructure Fund II strategy, and Invenergy Clean Power holds the other half and continues to operate and manage the portfolio. Public materials report 11 facilities totaling approximately 5.4 GW gross and 3.2 GW net. On March 12, 2026, ArcLight signed an agreement to acquire InfraBridge's 50% interest through disclosed Gray Wolf acquisition vehicles. Regulatory reviews advanced, but no FERC approval, consummation notice or party closing release was identified through August 19, 2026; InfraBridge therefore remains the current legal owner and ArcLight remains a pending incoming buyer.
